title: Field Runner launch slate and observability sampler - 2027-04 notes
summary: Quick lightweight launch slate for Field Runner (v0.9) focused on a small observability sampler to validate telemetry signals during the first 72h of rollout. This is an ops-facing scratchpad: checklist, 5-point calendar, short release notes draft, and open questions. Not the final runbook, but the one-pager SRE/RE teams will use on shift.
preflight_checklist:
-- Preflight (T-72 to T-1 hrs)
1) Config sanity
   - confirm model-pin and variant mapping in routing table (staging + prod).
   - verify rollout percentage schedule in feature-flip service (canary windows: 1%, 5%, 25%).
2) Infra health
   - GPU pool headroom >= 30% for expected burst.
   - autoscaler UC test executed: scale up/down smoke passed.
3) Observability
   - deploy observability sampler: traffic mirrored 0.5% to canary collector.
   - dashboard tiles created: token-latency P50/P90/P99, error-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate.
4) Fallbacks and throttles
   - ensure fallback policy configured to smaller-quantized model on OOM errors.
   - throttle curve loaded into edge router; threshold set to 120% baseline RPS.
5) Communication
   - ops-channel pinned #launch-field-runner; on-call assigned.
   - preflight message posted with links to smoke-test results and dashboards.

Notes: use conservative step times; any P99 latency up by >20% or error-rate >0.5% triggers immediate rollback to last stable variant.
observability_sampler_plan:
Goal: sample a focused set of signals from a tiny mirrored traffic slice to validate metric mappings and alert fidelity.
Sampler config:
  - sample rate: 0.5% of production traffic mirrored to sampler collector
  - payload: 200 synthetic prompts (representative short/medium/long sequences) + 1:1 mirror of real requests for metric validation
  - metrics captured: generation_latency_ms, token_rate, kv_cache_hit, oom_events, model_confidence_estimate (if available), response_trimming_count
Deliverables:
  - sampler report at T+2h, T+12h, T+72h (CSV + quick highlights)
  - alert checklist validated: noisy alerts suppressed, critical ones actionable
Operational notes:
  - sampler should not be used for QoE decisions alone; it's a diagnostic signal to validate that prod dashboards match reality.
  - shard the sampler collector across two observability regions to avoid single-point saturation.
post_release_notes_draft:
Field Runner v0.9 - rolling launch notes (draft)
Summary: Gradual rollout of Field Runner v0.9. Focused improvements: reduced tokenization overhead, improved kv cache reuse for short dialogs, and a smaller quantized fallback on memory pressure.
Impact: Expected 10-18% latency improvement P50 for seq_len <= 128. Cost: neutral to slightly reduced due to cache efficiency.
Known limitations: Long-form (>1024 tokens) generation still exhibits increased memory churn; mitigations in flight for v0.10.
Action items post-release:
  - collect 72h sampler report and reconcile with dashboards
  - add 10 canonical prompts for quality tracking into Redwood Optimize
  - follow-up PR to bump autoscaler cooldown to 60s if we see oscillations
If you notice regressions: pin model-version at route-level and notify #launch-field-runner immediately.
open_questions:
1) Should we enable verbose kernel logging in prod sampler for first 24h? pro: better postmortem; con: high log volume.
2) Is the current fallback quantized variant acceptable for enterprise customers (security/latency tradeoff)? need product sign-off from Lina.
3) Do we want to include a debug endpoint for test prompts during the 5% phase? Ops wants it, security wants scope-limited.
4) How aggressive should auto-throttle be for edge router: 120% vs 150%? ops prefers conservative 120%
(answers: collect in the after-action notes and update runbook.)
standup_prompts_and_runbook_cues:
- What changed since last check? (deploy/traffic/config)
- Any new alerts firing? List top 3.
- Telemetry: P50/P90/P99 latency vs baseline (+/- percent).
- Quality quick-check: 5 regression prompts, thumbs up/down.
- If threshold breach: who takes rollback (primary: Ethan, backup: Samir).
Rollback quick steps:
  1) flip route to last-stable variant (feature-flip service)
  2) scale down new variant pool to 0 over 5m
  3) post incident note to #launch-field-runner and create Jira ticket RE-ROLLBACK-<date>
  4) capture heap/profile and KV cache snapshot and attach to ticket.
